evidence.claim: A river mill village became a railway shipping point.
evidence.quote: The village of Rapid Ann Station resumed its prominence as a regional shipping point after the railroad was rebuilt following the Civil War

evidence.claim: Route 615 meets Routes 614 and 673 at Rapidan’s passenger depot.
evidence.quote: The Rapidan Passenger Depot is located at the junction of VA 614, VA 615, and VA 673 in Rapidan

evidence.claim: The village spans both banks of the Rapidan River, approximately five miles northeast of Orange.
evidence.quote: approximately five miles (8 km) northeast of the Town of Orange. The community, located on both sides of the Rapidan River

evidence.claim: Rapidan grew around the Waugh’s Ford mill in the late eighteenth century.
evidence.quote: was established in the late eighteenth century around the Waugh's Ford mill.

evidence.claim: The Orange and Alexandria Railroad arrived in 1854, and the settlement became Rapid Ann Station.
evidence.quote: The Orange and Alexandria Railroad built a line through the town in 1854, a post office was built at the river crossing, and its name was changed to Rapid Ann Station.

evidence.claim: After wartime destruction and railway rebuilding, it again shipped lumber and wood products.
evidence.quote: after the railroad was rebuilt following the Civil War, particularly for lumber and wood products.

evidence.claim: The name changed to Rapidan in 1886; milling continued into the mid-twentieth century.
evidence.quote: Its name was changed once again in 1886 to the present-day Rapidan.

evidence.claim: Begin at the depot junction in Rapidan, with Waddell Memorial Presbyterian Church nearby.
evidence.quote: Waddell Memorial Presbyterian Church is a historic Presbyterian church located near Rapidan

evidence.claim: Orange lies to the southwest.
evidence.quote: approximately five miles (8 km) northeast of the Town of Orange.

evidence.claim: There, the courthouse at Madison Road and Main Street marks another place reshaped by the railway.
evidence.quote: stands today on the corner of Madison Road and Main Street.

evidence.claim: milling continued into the mid-twentieth century.
evidence.quote: Milling remained a major industry in the area up through the mid-twentieth century.

evidence.claim: another place reshaped by the railway.
evidence.quote: The county court granted the railroad right-of-way through the courthouse property, which required the courthouse to be moved to another location.

evidence.claim: The depot stands at the meeting of Routes 614, 615 and 673, in a village whose name changed with the arrival of rail.
evidence.quote: The Rapidan Passenger Depot is located at the junction of VA 614, VA 615, and VA 673

evidence.claim: A station was established when the Orange and Alexandria Railroad reached the river in January 1854.
evidence.quote: In January 1854, the railroad reached the Rapidan River and a station was established.

evidence.claim: Waugh’s Ford became Rapid Ann Station, reflecting the river’s customary name.
evidence.quote: With the coming of the Orange and Alexandria Railroad in 1854, the settlement was renamed Rapid Ann Station, reflecting the customary name of the river

evidence.claim: Confederate cavalry burned the river bridge in April 1863; federal cavalry burned station facilities the following year.
evidence.quote: In April 1863, W.H.F. Lee's Confederate cavalry burnt the Rapidan River Bridge. In September 1864, the federal cavalry burnt facilities at Mitchell and Rapidan Stations.

evidence.claim: The village and station took the name Rapidan in 1886.
evidence.quote: In 1886, the village and the station was renamed Rapidan.

evidence.claim: Waddell Memorial’s tower arranges three features one above another: an arched doorway, a rose window and a belfry with paired pointed windows.
evidence.quote: a ground level with an equilateral-arched doorway, a middle level with a rose window, and a belfry with double pointed windows.

evidence.claim: Built in 1874, the frame church uses board-and-batten siding and Carpenter Gothic design.
evidence.quote: It was built in 1874, and is a Carpenter Gothic frame building covered with board-and-batten siding.

evidence.claim: The tower stands at the gable end.
evidence.quote: It features a three-stage tower at the gable end

evidence.claim: The church entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1975 and is part of the Rapidan Historic District.
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.  It is located in the Rapidan Historic District.

evidence.claim: The tower’s rose window sits between the arched doorway and the belfry.
evidence.quote: a ground level with an equilateral-arched doorway, a middle level with a rose window, and a belfry with double pointed windows.

evidence.claim: Orange’s courthouse moved to make room for the railroad.
evidence.quote: The county court granted the railroad right-of-way through the courthouse property, which required the courthouse to be moved to another location.

evidence.claim: In 1847, the Orange and Alexandria Railroad chose a route through town, and the county granted passage across the courthouse property.
evidence.quote: In 1847, the Orange and Alexandria Railroad chose to route their new railway from Alexandria to Gordonsville through Orange.

evidence.claim: The replacement, completed in 1859, stands at Madison Road and Main Street in the Italian Villa style.
evidence.quote: The fourth and current courthouse was completed in 1859 in the Italian Villa architectural style and stands today on the corner of Madison Road and Main Street.

evidence.claim: Its entrance arcade has a broad central arch flanked by two smaller arches.
evidence.quote: a three-part arcade consisting of a semi-elliptical arch flanked by small semicircular arches.

evidence.claim: The tower clock arrived later, fitted into existing round windows in 1949.
evidence.quote: a clock, installed within existing round windows in 1949

evidence.claim: After the Civil War, the rebuilt railroad helped the village resume its role as a shipping point for lumber and wood products.
evidence.quote: after the railroad was rebuilt following the Civil War, particularly for lumber and wood products.

evidence.claim: The courthouse complex also includes a clerk’s office dating to 1894 and a jail built in 1891, both contributing historic buildings.
evidence.quote: Associated with the courthouse are the contributing clerk's office (1894) and jail (1891).
